title: Canonical tame ramification sequence of a strictly henselian valuation trait
statement: Let $R$ be a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction field $K$ and residue field $k$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Let $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ be a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure] inside an algebraically closed field $\Omega$, and let $H=\operatorname{Gal}(K^{\mathrm{sep}}/K)$ with its profinite Krull topology. Put $p=1$ if $\operatorname{char}k=0$, and $p=\operatorname{char}k$ otherwise. For $(d,p)=1$, put $\mu_d(\Omega)=\{z\in\Omega^\times:z^d=1\}$, and let $G=\varprojlim_{(d,p)=1}\mu_d(\Omega)$, with transition $z\mapsto z^{e/d}$ for $d\mid e$ and inverse-limit topology. For a uniformizer $\pi$ choose compatible roots $\pi^{1/d}$. The maps $h\mapsto h(\pi^{1/d})/\pi^{1/d}$ define a continuous surjection $t:H\to G$ independent of these choices and of the uniformizer. Its kernel $S$ is a pro-$p$ group: each finite continuous quotient has $p$-power order; if $p=1$ then $S=1$. Thus $1\to S\to H\xrightarrow{t}G\to1$ is exact. The group $G$ is procyclic: compatible primitive roots give a topological generator $\sigma$, and for each $(d,p)=1$ the subgroup generated topologically by $\sigma^d$ has index $d$.

Its statement, stmt_deps and blueprint are identical to live, so the target is not weakened; only the split fields changed. The statement matches ILO XVII 1.2 (p.259): the canonical sequence 1→S→Gal→Ẑ'(1)→1 with S pro-p and p the characteristic exponent, and §1.2.1 uses the topological generator. The proof follows Stacks 0BUA/0BUB and 09EE. All hypotheses check: μ_d⊂R by henselian root lifting plus lem-sbc-strict-local-roots-of-unity; irreducibility of X^d−π by the root-algebra domain node; B_L is local by the henselian product node, with no excellence used; total inertia in both p>1 (pure inseparability) and p=1; e=d so α_d is a uniformizer; choice independence and surjectivity by gluing and extending from a normal subfield. For p>1, every hypothesis of the tower and inverse-limit nodes is checked, and the G≅C comparison is identified through K_d. For p=1, S=1 via the new node and the χ_L restriction formula. The CRT construction of primitive roots and the closure ⟨σ^d⟩=U_d with index d are both correct. The one new node, lem-per-dvr-char-zero-tangent-kernel (a finite-order, residue-trivial DVR automorphism with a(t)/t≡1 in residue characteristic 0 is the identity), is true by the 09EE(3) telescoping argument, and t↦t/(1+t) shows it fails in characteristic p. It is self-contained, not a clause of the item, and not a duplicate: every existing 09EE and tame node assumes p>0, and lem-exc-henselian-dvr-tame-sequence is excellent, algebraically-closed-residue and non-canonical. Its five Mathlib searches are logged. No SGA source is cited. I accept the nine declared tool_uses: generic algebra and profinite tools with no node in the perverse unit. Advisory, outside this delivery: lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product's source tag should be 00DT, not 00U3. No fixes.
